en: The *Sūtra on the Making of Buddha Images*, translated by an unknown name and recorded in the Later Han Catalogue, states:
When the Buddha arrived at the kingdom of Kuśinagara, there was a park owner named Kauśika. At that time, the king...
His name was Udayana, and he was fourteen years old.
Hearing that the Buddha was coming, the king immediately commanded his attendants and ministers to prepare the carriage; the king then set out himself to welcome the Buddha.
Seeing the Buddha from afar, his heart leaped with joy and delight.

The king immediately descended from his carriage and proceeded on foot; he dismissed his ministers and those attendants holding the parasol. The king hurried forward to meet the Buddha, prostrated himself with his head at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated the Buddha three times, knelt for a long time with palms joined, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Among the people of the heavens above and the world below, there is none who can equal the Buddha!”
Now the Buddha’s face, eyes, body, and conduct manifest forth; his radiance is so sublime and his beauty is thus wondrous that I never tire of beholding him.
Now the Buddha is the teacher of those above heaven and those below it among men; with a heart of compassion, he loves many.
The Buddha remained silent and did not respond. The king spoke to the Buddha again, saying:
"When a person performs wholesome deeds, where will they be reborn as a result of their merit?
After the Buddha has departed, I fear I shall no longer see him; therefore, I wish to create an image of the Buddha to pay homage to and serve."
"What kind of merit shall I obtain hereafter?
I pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will explain this for me; I wish to hear and know it.
The Buddha said:
“O young king!
What you have asked is most excellent!
Listen to my words.”
"Having heard it, you should keep it in your heart!
The King said, "Yes!"
“I shall receive your instruction.
The Buddha told the king:
“If you create images of the Buddha, I will explain to you in full the blessings and merits you shall obtain.”
The king said,
“I accept your grace!
The Buddha said:
“Those people in the world who fashion images of the Buddha will, in their future births, have pure and clear eyes, upright and handsome faces, and always possess beautiful bodies, hands, and feet.”
When born in the heavens, one will also be pure and clean, far surpassing the other devas, with beautiful eyes and countenance.
By creating an image of the Buddha, one obtains such merit.
By creating an image of the Buddha, wherever one is born, there shall be no ill-formed body; one’s physical form will be entirely complete and flawless.
After death, one will be reborn in the seventh Brahma Heaven, surpassing all other devas; with a countenance of peerless and exquisite beauty, one will be revered by all the gods.
Such is the merit obtained from creating an image of the Buddha.
“By fashioning images of the Buddha, one shall be born into a wealthy and noble family in future lives, being truly and utterly distinct from ordinary people of the world.
In whatever place one is born, one will not become the child of a poor household.”
The merit obtained by creating an image of the Buddha is as follows:
"One who creates an image of the Buddha will, in future lives, have a body that is constantly the color of purple-polished gold, with a countenance of incomparable beauty."

"By fashioning images of the Buddha, one will, in future births, be born into a wealthy family with immeasurable wealth and precious treasures, and will always be held in high esteem and loved by parents, brothers, and kinsmen."
The merit obtained from creating an image of the Buddha is as follows:

having created an image of the Buddha, one will be reborn in the world of Jambudvīpa in future lives, always being born into the families of emperors, kings, or nobles, and becoming a son in a virtuous and noble household.
The merit obtained from creating an image of the Buddha is such as this.

By creating an image of the Buddha, one will become a sovereign among emperors in future lives, being the most honored and supreme among all kings, and one to whom all other kings look up with reverence.
The merit obtained by creating an image of the Buddha is such as this.

By creating an image of the Buddha, one will become a Cakravartin King in a future life; after ascending to the heavens, one shall descend again at will, performing whatever deeds one desires, reaching everywhere without exception.
The merit obtained by creating an image of the Buddha is like this:
after death, one will be born in the seventh Brahma Heaven, where one’s lifespan will last for one kalpa, and no one will be able to equal one’s wisdom.
“By fashioning images of the Buddha, after death one will no longer be reborn in the evil realms.
Those who are born [in good realms] shall always maintain their integrity;
their minds will constantly desire to seek the path of the Buddha.”
The merit obtained by creating an image of the Buddha is as follows:

"By creating an image of the Buddha, one will be born in future lives always revering the Buddha and possessing a compassionate heart toward the sutras. Constantly offering various silks and brocades, fine flowers, exquisite incense, lighting lamps, and presenting all manner of rare treasures and extraordinary objects from the heavens to the relics of the Buddha, after innumerable kalpas, one shall surely attain the Way of Nirvana."
If there are people who, with sincere intent, present precious treasures to the Buddha, none of them are ordinary persons; they have practiced the path of the Buddha in previous lives.
Such is the merit obtained by creating images of the Buddha.
“By creating images of the Buddha, one shall obtain merit in future lives that is inexhaustible and beyond end, such that it cannot be calculated by number.
The rivers and the waters of the oceans within the four continents may yet be measured with a peck and dried up;
however, the merit obtained from creating images of the Buddha exceeds ten times the volume of the rivers and the waters of the oceans of the four continents.”
Those born in future generations will be respected and protected by others.
"To create an image of the Buddha is like rain falling from the heavens upon a person who has a fine house; they have nothing to fear."
“By fashioning images of the Buddha, one will not, after death in a future life, be reborn again in the evil realms of hell, as a bird or beast, or as a hungry ghost.

Furthermore, if there are those who see an image of the Buddha and, with a heart of compassion, join their palms in homage and take refuge in the Buddha’s stūpa or relics, they shall not enter hell, the animal realm, or the realm of hungry ghosts for a hundred kalpas after death; upon dying, they will immediately be reborn in the heavens.”

When his lifespan in heaven comes to an end, he will descend again to be born in the world as the son of a wealthy family; his treasures and rare objects will be beyond counting, and thereafter he shall surely attain the path of the Buddha’s nirvāṇa.
The Buddha told the king:
"O doer of good!
The blessings and merit one obtains from fashioning an image of the Buddha are thus; they are not in vain."
The king was filled with joy; he stepped forward and paid homage to the Buddha, touching his head and face to the Buddha’s feet.
The king and his ministers all paid homage to the Buddha and departed.
When their lives ended, they were all reborn in the land of Amitābha Buddha.
This is from the *Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Making Images of the Buddha*.
